classification.classification_note: The saved failure is an ASan `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read`, but the underlying memory-safety error is the negative `time_units` array index created by the swapped reverse-time guard/index pairing in `reverse_obs`.

bug_description.original: The vulnerability allows array lookup with wrong indices due to missing validation before accessing the array.
bug_description.normalized: The exact 682-byte `standard_fuzzer` witness is split into a source proj string, a destination proj string, and trailing coordinate bytes. Replaying `pj_init_plus_ctx()` on the saved destination line yields a first `proj=` token of `ob_tran`, a wrapper token `o_proj=pipeline`, a nested `proj=pipeline` definition, and a final step-specific sequence containing `inv`, `+proj=unitconvert`, and `t_out=decimalyear`; the file contains no `t_in=` substring anywhere. The top-level destination object is therefore `ob_tran`, which builds a linked `pipeline`; that pipeline copies the final step's step-specific args before inherited global args, so its nested `pj_init()` materializes a `unitconvert` step rather than the later global `proj=hgridshift` garbage. `PROJECTION(unitconvert)` leaves `Q->t_in_id = -1` and resolves `Q->t_out_id` to the `decimalyear` entry. During `pj_transform()` the destination forward path reaches that step through pipeline inverse dispatch, and vulnerable `reverse_obs()` checks `Q->t_out_id >= 0` but indexes `time_units[Q->t_in_id]`, turning state `(-1, 1)` into `time_units[-1].t_out(...)` and the saved ASan wild-address read.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled destination projection definition into mutable parser storage.
source.value_from: In the exact witness, the destination definition is line 2 (bytes 241-673). Replaying the vulnerable splitter over that line yields a first `proj=` token `proj=ob_tran`, then `o_proj=pipeline`, `proj=pipeline`, and a final step-specific `inv`, `+proj=unitconvert`, `t_out=decimalyear` sequence; no `t_in=` substring exists anywhere in the file.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The second reverse-time branch validates `Q->t_out_id` but indexes `time_units` with `Q->t_in_id`. When only `t_out` is configured, the guard still passes even though the indexed `t_in_id` sentinel remains `-1`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix swaps the reverse branches back to the correct pairing, so `Q->t_out_id` guards/indexes the `t_in` conversion and `Q->t_in_id` guards/indexes the `t_out` conversion.

sink.description: Sink. With `Q->t_in_id == -1`, this expression reads the `t_out` function pointer from `time_units[-1]` and immediately calls it, producing the saved wild-address read / SEGV.
sink.note: Stage 01's ASan trace only exposes `_fini`, but this is the only staged negative `time_units[]` access whose guard/index state matches the witness and the patch hunk.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled `t_out=decimalyear` token is resolved to a concrete `time_units` table index and stored in `Q->t_out_id`. The paired `Q->t_in_id` stays at `-1` because no `t_in` token exists in the witness or in the reconstructed unitconvert step args.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The last pipeline step reconstructed from line 2 passes `proj=unitconvert` and `t_out=decimalyear` to nested `pj_init()` before any inherited global `proj=` token, and the exact witness contains no `t_in=` substring.

parser_admitted.description: The copied destination definition survives tokenization and is admitted as a top-level `ob_tran` object. Later wrapper parsing, not direct top-level selection, consumes `o_proj=pipeline`, the nested `step` markers, and the eventual `unitconvert` step.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer trace is under-symbolized: the only runtime frame is `_fini` in `/out/standard_fuzzer`, so the source-line sink is grounded from the staged source, patch hunk, and the statically replayed witness state rather than a direct source-level crash stack.

Large parts of the destination definition are fuzz-corrupted. Static replay deterministically recovers the load-bearing wrapper tokens (`proj=ob_tran`, `o_proj=pipeline`, `proj=pipeline`, `inv`, `+proj=unitconvert`, `t_out=decimalyear`) and proves the absence of `t_in=`, but it does not assign semantics to every corrupted non-matching token.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 does not measure whether `ob_tran` executed `o_forward` or `t_forward`; both installed forward arms delegate to `Q->link->fwd`, so this residual ambiguity does not alter the closed sink path.

fine_trace.note: Source. `pj_init_plus_ctx()` copies the attacker-controlled destination definition into mutable parser storage. Replaying this exact line through the vulnerable splitter yields first `proj=ob_tran`, then `o_proj=pipeline`, then `proj=pipeline`, and a final step-specific `inv`, `+proj=unitconvert`, `t_out=decimalyear` sequence; the witness contains no `t_in=` substring.

Top-level projection selection consumes the first matching `proj=` token in the copied destination definition. Because `pj_param()` returns the first match, this selects `ob_tran`; the later nested `proj=pipeline` and `+proj=unitconvert` tokens are not the top-level projection.

Inside the selected `ob_tran` constructor, `pj_param(..., "so_proj")` consumes the wrapper token `o_proj=pipeline`, choosing `pipeline` as the linked projection that will receive the same parameter list.

The `ob_tran` wrapper stores the original param list on `Q->link` and initializes that linked object as a `pipeline`, preserving all later `step`, `inv`, `proj=unitconvert`, and `t_out=decimalyear` tokens for nested parsing.

When the linked pipeline builds its last step, it copies the step-specific tokens before any global pipeline tokens. Static replay of the saved line shows that this last step contributes `inv`, `+proj=unitconvert`, and `t_out=decimalyear`, so the later step-local `proj=unitconvert` appears in `current_argv` before inherited global `proj=hgridshift` garbage.
The copied `inv` token marks this unitconvert step for inverse dispatch, so later forward pipeline execution will call the step through `PJ_INV` rather than `PJ_FWD`.

The pipeline materializes the step by calling `pj_init(current_argc, current_argv)`. During that nested init, `pj_mkparam()` strips the extra leading `+` from `+proj=unitconvert`, `pj_param(..., "sproj")` sees `proj=unitconvert` as the first matching step projection, and `PROJECTION(unitconvert)` is instantiated for this pipeline slot.
The unitconvert constructor starts with both time-unit IDs disabled. With no `t_in=` token anywhere in the witness or the reconstructed step args, `Q->t_in_id` stays at the sentinel `-1`.

The same constructor does find the step-specific `t_out=decimalyear`, resolves it in `time_units[]`, and stores the corresponding index in `Q->t_out_id`; the live pair is now `(Q->t_in_id, Q->t_out_id) = (-1, 1)`.

At runtime the harness calls `pj_transform(pj_src, pj_dst, ...)`. On the destination side, `pj_transform()` enters `pj_fwd(..., dstdefn)` for the top-level `ob_tran` object; ordinary wrapper math is omitted here, but its installed forward callback delegates into the linked pipeline created at step 4.

Within pipeline forward execution, the unitconvert slot is reached and the `reverse_step` flag from step 6 takes the inverse arm, issuing `proj_trans_obs(..., PJ_INV, point)` on the nested unitconvert object.

Inverse observation dispatch calls the step's `P->invobs` callback. For the object created at step 7, `PROJECTION(unitconvert)` installed `P->invobs = reverse_obs`, so control enters the vulnerable reverse time-conversion routine.
Root cause. The reverse-time branch uses `Q->t_out_id` as the guard but `Q->t_in_id` as the array index. With step 9's state, `Q->t_out_id >= 0` succeeds even though `Q->t_in_id` is still `-1`.
Sink. This expression reads `time_units[-1].t_out` and immediately calls it, matching the saved ASan `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` even though the runtime stack is under-symbolized to `_fini`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Partially. The saved ASan report only exposes `_fini` / `wild-addr-read`, but the staged patch and the statically replayed `ob_tran -> pipeline -> unitconvert -> reverse_obs` chain show line 317 is the only staged negative `time_units[]` access compatible with the witness's `t_out`-without-`t_in` state.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Partially. The runtime stack does not name project frames, but the staged source closes a deterministic path from the saved destination line through wrapper parsing, nested pipeline step creation, inverse dispatch, and the fixed line-317 read.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The second witness line creates a reverse-dispatched unitconvert step with `Q->t_out_id = 1` and no `t_in`, and those exact values are the guard/index pair consumed at the line-317 sink.

format.name: standard_fuzzer 3-line projection input
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact 682-byte `standard_fuzzer` witness used in Stage 01. The vulnerability-relevant contract is only what the saved bytes prove: line 2 tokenizes to a top-level `proj=ob_tran` definition with `o_proj=pipeline`, a nested `proj=pipeline`, and a final step-specific `inv`, `+proj=unitconvert`, `t_out=decimalyear` sequence, while the file contains no `t_in=` substring. Source-grounded analysis does not generalize beyond that exact witness.
